newsitem.title: USA: Huizenga's Florida Panthers to buy Florida hotel.
newsitem.headline: Huizenga's Florida Panthers to buy Florida hotel.

text.p: Billionaire investor H. Wayne Huizenga's Florida Panthers Holdings Inc. said Wednesday it will buy a controlling stake in a luxury Florida hotel from the privately held Leehill Group for $75 million in cash.

The purchase of the Registry Hotel in Naples, Fla., brings the company, which owns the Florida Panthers hockey team, another step toward its goal of becoming a "diversified leisure-time sports and entertainment company," it said.
The deal also calls for Florida Panthers Holdings to issue 930,000 shares of Class A common stock, subject to some lock-up restrictions for up to two years.
Panther Holdings also owns interests in the Florida Panthers hockey team's arena and has purchased three other Florida hotels since it went public in November at $10 a share.
The stock slipped 37.5 cents to $23.625 in early afternoon trading. It currently trades on the Nasdaq but will begin trading Friday on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol "PAW".

"We are very pleased with this transaction, which adds to the company a very profitable and prestigious asset. ... We are continuing to explore other high-quality opportunities in luxury resorts and club properties," said Huizenga, chairman of Florida Panthers Holdings.
The company also filed for a secondary offering of up to 6 million shares of Class A stock, it said.
